subject.title: feat(plugins): upgrade llm_input/llm_output hooks from fire-and-forget to modifying

question: Should the shipped `llm_input` and `llm_output` observer hooks remain non-blocking, with new modifying hooks added separately, or should OpenClaw intentionally version and migrate those existing hook names into an awaited control contract?
rationale: This is a permanent plugin API and trust-boundary choice: source compatibility for `void` returns does not preserve the existing timing, failure, and runner-consistency contract.

options.title: Add separate modifying hooks
options.body: Keep the existing observer hooks fire-and-forget and introduce explicitly named awaited modifying hooks with clear runner coverage and documentation.

options.title: Version the existing hook names
options.body: Accept the behavior change only with an explicit SDK compatibility plan, upgrade documentation, and implementation in every supported runner.

recommendation.title: Add separate modifying hooks
recommendation.body: Keep the existing observer hooks fire-and-forget and introduce explicitly named awaited modifying hooks with clear runner coverage and documentation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the original observer-hook contract in the merged feature history.
